sections.heading: After the New Roof Goes On
body: **We don't leave when the last shingle goes down.** Our crew walks around your house for anything that fell off the roof, and we've come back after the crew left just to make sure a homeowner was pleased.
**We've handled the insurance side too.** When a claim was behind one new roof, we talked with the homeowner's insurance agent and got the forms filled out and returned.

sections.quote: After they finished, they walked around to make sure if anything fell off the roof that everything was picked up.  Anthony showed up shortly after they left to make sure I was pleased with the roof.  Anthony handled talking to my insurance agent and getting forms filed out and returned to them.

sections.heading: Composition Shingles, Metal or Tile
body: **We install composition shingles, metal roofing and tile.** At the quote, we go over which of the three suits your house, how you want it to look and what you want to spend.
**We help you choose, down to the shingle and the color.** Our job is to give you enough information to make the decision that suits you, not to push one product.

sections.heading: When a New Roof Makes Sense
body: **A new roof makes sense when the trouble isn't in one spot anymore.** Leaks that come back after repairs, damage across several parts of the roof, or worn shingles all over mean more patching is money spent twice.
**One bad spot is a repair, and we tell you so.** If a [roof repair](/roof-repair-wichita-ks/) solves the problem, that's the job we quote.

You want a different material, like metal or tile

sections.heading: We Find Where the Water Really Comes In
body: **A leak shows up in one spot and starts in another.** So we go into the attic and onto the roof to trace it before we quote a fix.
That's how a stain on a kitchen ceiling turned out to be a leaking chimney chase, not the roof. You pay to fix the real problem, not the one that looked likely.

sections.quote: We had a leak in the kitchen ceiling. We assumed it was from the roof so we called a slew of different contractors. We ended up going with River City Roofing as Anthony crawled into the attic and onto the roof and found that our CHIMNEY CHASE was leaking.
sections.name: Brant C.

footer.about: We're a local, family owned roofing company in Wichita. We replace and repair roofs, and we do siding, gutters, paint, windows and deck staining.
why: We find the real source of a leak

Your customers make your case. All nine of your Google reviews are five stars, and the written ones keep naming Anthony: he climbed into an attic to find a leaking chimney chase, dealt with an insurance agent, and came back after the crew left to check on a new roof.
Your website shows none of it. Its tap-to-call links dial 123-456-7890, and no page has a headline that says you're a roofing company in Wichita.
So we built this site around their words.
strategy.cardsHeading: Be the Roofing Company People Find on Google
strategy.cardsIntro: Each card is one page: what your site does today, and what we changed.

cards.title: Homepage
cards.why: The page Google reads to learn who you are and where you work.
problems: The tap-to-call links at the bottom of every page dial 123-456-7890, and the number at the top can't be tapped, so nobody on a phone can call you in one tap.
No page shows a headline. The hidden one Google reads says "Home", so it can't tell you're a roofing company in Wichita.
None of your Google reviews appear on the site, so visitors never see what your customers say.
fixes: Your number is one tap to call, on every page.
A headline that says roofing company in Wichita, KS, right at the top.
Real reviews from your customers, each beside the point it proves.
cards.alsoAdd: Every page set up behind the scenes so Google and AI tools like ChatGPT know exactly what you do, where you work, and what your customers say.

cards.title: Roof Replacement
cards.why: A new roof is a big decision, and it has no page of its own.
problems: One "Roofing" page covers every kind of roof job, so someone searching for roof replacement in Wichita doesn't land on a page about it.
It never shows what your customers praise: the cleanup and the visit after the crew leaves.
fixes: A full page for roof replacement in Wichita, KS: materials, the detailed estimate and the steps of the job.
The cleanup and the visit afterward, with the review that proves them.
cards.alsoAdd: Pages planned from what Google actually shows for each search, so every page targets something people really look for.

cards.title: Roof Repair
cards.why: Your customers praise how you handled leaks and wind damage, and repair has no page either.
problems: Roof repair sits as one line on the "Roofing" page, so Google has nothing to rank for a leak or storm damage search.
fixes: A full page for roof repair in Wichita, KS, with the chimney chase leak and the wind damage told in your customers' words.
cards.alsoAdd: A check of what your competitors offer, so services you didn’t think to mention still get their own pages.

cards.title: Contact
cards.why: Where a ready customer reaches you.
problems: The number at the bottom dials a placeholder, and the number on your roofing page can't be tapped.
fixes: Your real number one tap away, with your hours, your address and what to have ready.
cards.alsoAdd: Call and form tracking that shows which pages and towns your leads come from.

reportCard.label: Headline says what you do and where

closing.heading: Want a website like this for your business?
closing.text: Book a strategy call with Fluid Frame, and we'll walk you through this demo and plan your new site.

onboardingQuestions: Who is Anthony (owner, partner, manager), and what is his surname? Can the site name him and say how he is introduced?
Who is the owner? BuildZoom lists Wilbur Engel; the site names no one. May we use the name?
Legal name: River City Roofing, LLC (site footer) or Honey Do Homes, LLC dba River City Roofing (logo and BuildZoom)?
Since when? The site says 2011; listings say 13 years, 14 years and 2003. No founding year is on the demo until confirmed.
Certifications: GAF (which level, contractor number), Andersen, Pella and CAPS. Proof for each, or we drop them. None is on the demo.
BBB, Wichita Chamber and WABA: are they members, and can we show it?
Kansas roofing licence CT-13-116090: active or expired?
Phone: (316) 295-2159 is on the demo. Does (316) 312-8657 (BuildZoom, Houzz) go to the office?
Email address for the business? None is shown on the site.
Insurance help: one customer (Kamden B.) had Anthony handle the agent and forms. Do you offer that to every roof customer? The demo calls it track record only.
Warranty, financing and free inspections: do you offer them? None is on the demo (free quote only).
Service area: Wichita only, or do you travel to nearby towns? The site says "throughout Kansas" with no towns.
Hours: Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM, no weekend or storm-call hours?
Services to confirm: roof maintenance, gutters and guards, painting, windows, deck staining. Which are the biggest earners, and should any get its own page?
Photos of real jobs, and the owner's okay to use the Google reviews on the site.

Cleanup and the visit after the job: does the crew walk the yard for debris, and does someone come back after every new roof? The demo states cleanup and a final inspection as how a new roof goes, and the return visit only as track record (Kamden B.).
Painters: your own crew or another company you send? The demo avoids saying one crew does everything.
Can customers text (316) 295-2159? A review mentions texting Anthony; the demo says call only.
Routine roof maintenance: what does a visit include, and how is it priced?
